question: What is “class imbalance” in a classification dataset?

options.B: When one or more classes have significantly fewer samples than others, which can bias the model toward the majority class
options.C: A technique for balancing computational load across GPUs
options.D: A method for normalizing feature values

question: What is “feature engineering”?

options.A: The process of designing and transforming raw data into features that better represent the underlying problem to a model
options.B: The process of installing GPUs onto a server
options.C: The process of writing the model's architecture code
options.D: The process of labeling a dataset manually

question: Which of the following are valid reasons to use the F1 score instead of accuracy alone?

options.A: When classes are imbalanced, accuracy can be misleading
options.B: F1 score balances precision and recall in a single metric
options.C: F1 score is always higher than accuracy
options.D: F1 score is useful when both false positives and false negatives matter

question: Which of the following statements about data preprocessing are true?

options.A: Machine learning tasks generate results in the form of model outputs, so model training is more important than data preprocessing
options.B: Data standardization aims to reduce noise data and improve model accuracy
options.C: Data cleansing is the process of filling in missing values and detecting/eliminating noise and exceptions
options.D: Data dimension reduction aims to simplify data attributes and avoid the curse of dimensionality

question: Which of the following best describes “precision” in classification evaluation?

options.A: The proportion of actual positive instances that were correctly identified
options.B: The proportion of instances predicted as positive that are actually positive
options.C: The overall proportion of correct predictions across all classes
options.D: The average error between predicted and actual continuous values

question: Which of the following can cause a machine learning model to perform poorly on real-world data despite good training accuracy?

options.A: Overfitting to the training set
options.B: Data leakage between training and test sets
options.C: Using cross-validation properly during development
options.D: A shift between the training data distribution and the real-world data distribution

question: What is the purpose of splitting a dataset into training, validation, and test sets?

options.A: To increase the total amount of data available
options.B: To estimate how well a model generalizes to unseen data, while keeping tuning decisions separate from final evaluation
options.C: To make the model train faster
options.D: To eliminate the need for labels

question: Which metric is most appropriate for evaluating a regression model's prediction error?

options.A: Accuracy
options.B: F1 score
options.C: Mean Squared Error (MSE)

question: In a confusion matrix for binary classification, what does a “false positive” represent?

options.A: A negative instance correctly predicted as negative
options.B: A positive instance correctly predicted as positive
options.C: A negative instance incorrectly predicted as positive
options.D: A positive instance incorrectly predicted as negative

question: Why is data normalization/standardization often applied before training a model?

options.A: To increase the number of features
options.B: To bring different features onto comparable scales, helping optimization converge more reliably
options.C: To remove all correlation between features
options.D: To convert categorical data into images

question: Which of the following best describes “recall” in classification evaluation?

options.A: The proportion of instances predicted as positive that are actually positive
options.B: The proportion of actual positive instances that were correctly identified by the model
options.C: The total number of predictions made
options.D: The ratio of true negatives to false positives
